title: Consolidate CI tasks into a lightweight 'ci-condenser' and route slow suites to smoke lane
author: Evan Park
description: Motivation: our premerge CI runtime is drifting higher as we add more integration-level checks. This PR introduces a small Go-based helper (tools/ci-condenser) plus workflow adjustments that condense redundant setup steps, de-duplicates dependency bootstraps across matrix cells, and automatically routes deterministic fast suites to premerge lanes while moving long-running or non-deterministic tests into a 'smoke' lane that runs on a fast-path nightlies or when touched-files heuristics indicate affected runtime. Scope: add ci-condenser binary with basic manifest parsing and caching hooks; change .github workflows to call ci-condenser for job orchestration; add tagging for tests in ci/slow-tests.csv and a smoke-runner script; refactor existing bash bootstraps into a single Makefile target and a Go entrypoint to improve hermeticity; trim devdeps and move heavy integration-only deps behind the smoke lane so premerge artifacts are smaller. Checklist: - [x] Implement ci-condenser binary and unit tests - [x] Wire workflows to use condensed steps and cache warmers - [x] Add slow-tests CSV and smoke runner script - [x] Update developer docs in docs/ci/ci-condenser.md - [x] Run canary on infra repo and fix flakiness notes Impact/risk: lightweight change to CI orchestration only, runtime code untouched; risk of test misclassification which is mitigated by a default-all-fast fallback and an opt-in smoke label. Rollout plan: feature branch merges to main with staged rollout: enable condensed runs for a subset of repos, monitor CI latency and failure modes for 72 hours, flip default. Related: ENG-1429 (CI latency spike), ENG-1501 (slow-tests reclassification).

review_comments: Sara Liu: Overall a big win on CI latency reduction, nice work. Small request: can ci-condenser emit a deterministic job fingerprint so we can easily tie cache keys to a specific run? Also add more unit coverage around the touched-files heuristic.

Evan Park: Added deterministic fingerprint generation and extended unit tests for the touched-files matcher. Fingerprint uses SHA256 of normalized manifest and commit metadata. See commit b3d5f20 and tests in tools/ci-condenser/.
Rajat Mehra: I saw a flaky failure on the smoke runner in the first CI attempt — the post-teardown sometimes left docker artifacts. Could we add a stricter cleanup and retry on network pulls?
Evan Park: Added exponential-backoff for docker pulls and ensured full cleanup in scripts/run-smoke.sh. Also added a canary run in a staging repo which passed twice in a row.
Olivia Grant: Minor docs nits: clarify when to mark a test as slow and add example labels. Fixed in docs/ci/ci-condenser.md. Approving pending a passing CI run.
release_notes: Introduce ci-condenser to centralize CI setup and reduce duplicate bootstrap work across matrix jobs.
Add smoke lane for slow/non-deterministic tests and reclassify heavy integration deps.
Trim dev dependencies and move integration-only deps behind the smoke nightly to speed premerge feedback.
notes: Observed ~28% median CI latency reduction in initial canary across three repos. Follow-up: monitor false-negatives from heuristic and add telemetry for test promotions.
